notes:
Lead: mid-market product analytics platform. Initial host trial ran Jan 25–Feb 28 (free credits). Team: Head of Product (Maya Ortiz), ML Eng (Liam Duarte), Infra Eng (Sana Rao).

Quick summary / vibe: strong technical, cost-conscious, wants predictable latency for interactive product assistant and cheaper embeddings for large-scale search index. Interested in Hosted first (fast POC) then Dedicated for production once throughput/p99s are validated.

POC highlights: saw 30–60 QPS baseline on Hosted during simulated user traffic, spikes to ~110 QPS during scheduled load tests (20:00 PST). Average conversation token mix observed: prompt 60 tokens, generation 140 tokens for chat assistant; normalization: ~1.5mb payload/day for embeddings jobs. Embedding calls were high-volume but low latency requirement (batching ok).

Customer-supplied metrics (trial):
- Avg QPS (workday): 42
- Peak QPS (load test): 112
- 95p latency target: <= 250ms for chat front-door
- Concurrent open sessions: 210 (concurrent users during peak window)
- Token mix: 60% short-chat (<=200 tokens total), 30% mid (200-800 tokens), 10% long (>800 tokens) — long tail mostly agent-initiated reports
- Embeddings: ~120k vectors/day (1M requests/week), median vector size 1536 dims

Key asks from PLS:
- Dedicated capacity sizing: what GPU pool(s) to recommend for sustained 50 QPS with headroom to 150 QPS? (they want per-GPU QPS estimate + cost delta vs Hosted).
- Token accounting: per-request distribution and suggested batching strategies to hit cost targets.
- Routing/fallback plan: inexpensive smaller model fallback for non-critical path (query rewriting, reranking) and canary rollout for model upgrades.
- Residency and logs: logs must remain in EU region for EU customers; product telemetry can be aggregated to NA.

Call notes (ff_20260218):
- Maya: "We loved the API speed on the trial but need predictable SLA and cost for holiday spikes."
- Liam: asked for guidance on KV cache sizing and prefix caching for conversational sessions.
- Sana: wants a simple autoscale recipe (min nodes, burst policy) and recommended GPU types.

Internal AE/se annotation:
- Sent initial sizing spreadsheet Mar 3 (drive link). Waiting on Redwood Dedicated sizing template with per-GPU token/sec. SE asked infra metrics export from PLS (prod logs sample) — PLS to share by Mar 9.

POC outcomes so far:
- Hosted API worked functionally for all use-cases (chat, embedding, reranking).
- Cost at Hosted trial is acceptable short-term, but projected 6-12 month spend >$100k unless embeddings are batched/quantized.
- Team leaning toward Dedicated reservation if Redwood can show 20-30% unit-cost reduction + clear SLA for 95p latencies.

Suggested Dedicated sizing (from SE call, provisional):
- Baseline sustained: target 50 QPS (conservative avg) -> 2 x A40-equivalent GPUs with autoscale to 6 GPUs for burst to 150 QPS.
- Preferred production config (high availability + headroom): 4 x A100-40GB (or 6 x A10G) depending on model quantization; includes KV cache nodes for long-conversation state.
- Embeddings: dedicated batch worker pool (2x smaller GPUs) with scheduled batch windows for index rebuilds to minimize cost.
- Fallback model plan: rM-compat small model for rerank/heuristics to reduce cost on non-critical traffic.

Commercial notes:
- Customer requested 12-month committed pricing and a trial extension (30 days) for Dedicated pilot. Wants clear overage pricing.
- Estimated ARR ask: they expect first-year Redwood spend in the $40k–$120k range depending on cluster sizing and batching effectiveness.
